conventions.convention: Heat is positive into the working system and work-on is positive into it. Engine mode has Q[P]=Q_h−Q_c and W_on=−W_out; refrigerator mode has Q[P]=Q_c−Q_h and W_on=W_in. The ideal work store has zero entropy change and receives W_out or supplies W_in.

Ideal baths have exactly affine entropy S_b(E)=s_b,0+E/T_b on their admitted energy intervals. The full compound has an admitted isolated process record, matching constituent endpoints, and an explicitly additive entropy split; unlisted transfers are excluded.

Both bounds require 0<T_c<T_h and positive heat and work magnitudes. Equality is equivalent to zero total compound entropy change; reversibility implies equality, but the converse about reversibility is not asserted.

Nernst is adopted as uniform vanishing of entropy differences over a specified nonempty compact label space. Continuity in the label is not assumed; sufficiently small-temperature suprema must be finite. Individual finite entropy limits and an absolute zero entropy normalization are not supplied.

Operational unattainability concerns every finite compatible chain in the full declared operation family on a disjoint positive-temperature domain and nonempty zero-temperature boundary. Excluding boundary endpoints by the operation definition makes the assertion vacuous.

The heat-capacity bound uses the dimensionless variable θ=T/T_* and every real exponent q≥1; its big-O coefficient has units J/K. The witness is a formal local response chart, without a global bulk-family or empirical realization claim.

The finite canonical model adopts normalized Gibbs weights and Gibbs entropy with the SI Boltzmann constant and natural logarithm. Its positive Kelvin-valued parameter is not identified with macroscopic entropy-derived temperature. The finite ground-state multiplicity is g≥1, with a positive gap to any excited states.

Geometric cooling uses only f(T)=rT on D_+=(0,T_*], with 0<r<1 and fixed positive finite operation duration. Natural-number lengths include zero, whose endpoint is the stipulated initial coordinate; the coordinate is not identified with thermodynamic temperature.

load_bearing.statement: A two-reservoir cycle consists of one working-system cycle, one hot bath at T_h, one cold bath at T_c, and the ideal work store, inside an isolated outer boundary with no unlisted transfers. Bath entropy changes are exactly their energy changes divided by their fixed positive temperatures, and the work store has zero entropy change.

For an admitted heat-engine cycle with 0<T_c<T_h, Q_h>0, Q_c>0 and W_out>0, η=W_out/Q_h≤1−T_c/T_h. Equality holds exactly when the isolated compound's total entropy change is zero. A reversible cycle saturates the bound; zero entropy change is not asserted to imply full reversibility.

For an admitted refrigerator cycle with 0<T_c<T_h, Q_c>0, Q_h>0 and W_in>0, COP_R=Q_c/W_in≤T_c/(T_h−T_c). Equality holds exactly when the isolated compound's total entropy change is zero. A reversible cycle saturates the bound; no converse about reversibility is asserted.

For the declared positive-temperature equilibrium family indexed by nonempty compact K, the model adopts lim as t↓0 of sup over a,b∈K of |S_K(t,a)−S_K(t,b)|=0. Individual finite entropy limits are additional premises.

For the declared state extension and full family C of admitted finite-duration operations, Reach_C∩(D_c,+×D_0)=∅ is adopted as a separate physical assumption. Empty relevant domains or exclusion of boundary endpoints by construction give an absent or vacuous assertion.

concerns.concern: The page writes the Gibbs entropy limit as '(k_{\mathrm B}\log g)' without dollar delimiters. This leaves the LaTeX commands as plain page prose rather than rendered mathematics. The corresponding item states the correct formula with math delimiters.
